title: HLabs: unembed plu-ts - the next aiken

ms.promise:
a Tokenizer class taking as input the source text and with the necessary methods to emit the tokens of the language
this is the first step of the compiler, where from a raw piece of text we get something that is more easy to work with "tokens", wich are nothing more than smaller pieces of text that carry some meaning on their own (eg. words).
The output of this milestone is the implementation of this first part of the compiler
ms.criteria:
given some text (the source code) the tokenizer can iter over it emitting the corresponding tokens
for example the text "const thing = 2;" will produce the tokens "const" "identifier" "thing" "equals" "literal integer" "2" "semicolon".
ms.report:
the implemented Tokenizer can be found here: https://github.com/HarmonicLabs/pebble/blob/main/packages/pebble/src/tokenizer/Tokenizer.ts
here is a video showcasing how the Tokenizer is used: https://youtu.be/51q2KN11pf8

ms.promise:
a class that takes as input a Tokenizer from the previous milestone and consumes the emitted tokens to build an AST representation of the source language.
during construction of the AST, the parser makes sure that the syntax of the language is respected.
at this point the compiler starts making some sense of the source code
here syntatic errors are catched, for example "const thing = 2;" is valid syntax, but "const const = 2;" is not, because "const" is a keyword of the language and cannot be used for the name of a variable.
ms.criteria:
given a source text it is possible to build the AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) representation of it.
The AST is just an in-memory representation of the source code. where the pieces of text are "grouped" based on known structures.
so at this point, the compiler is able to "see" these structures and store them in variables.
ms.report:
here is the Parser implementation: https://github.com/HarmonicLabs/pebble/blob/main/packages/pebble/src/parser/Parser.ts
here is a video showcasing how the Parser works: https://youtu.be/qD7hACz5W2Q

ms.promise:
From the AST we proceed to check the semantic of the program and compile it to a lower level intermediate representation (IR) used to further optimize the contract.

This steps includes:
・Type checking
・desugaring (for loops etc.)
・rewriting expression in semantic equivalent
・etc.

Here the compiler has the full picture of the program and is able to finally "translate" the source code to something closer to the language of the blockchain (uplc)
ms.criteria:
The IR (and UPLC as consequence) is built from a program
At this point the compiler is able to produce valid contracts that can be used on-chain
ms.report:
here is the Compiler implementation: https://github.com/HarmonicLabs/pebble/blob/main/packages/pebble/src/compiler/Compiler.ts
here is a video showcasing how the compiler works: https://youtu.be/gOXJvO2fZb0
